Canrenoic acid, in turn, is predicted to target HaCaT, indicating a possible downstream effect of the compound on the cell line. The scores suggest a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction. The mechanism likely involves the compound modulating the activity of the neuronal receptor, which may influence cellular processes in HaCaT cells. The evidence highlights a potential pathway where the compound could exert its effects through the neuronal receptor, but the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated.
